cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Keep the spare cupboard key till tomorrow. Don't tell your flatmate I've left it here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell me what's in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Could you accept knowing what isn't? Nothing alive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you collect it before she gets home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Text me when she leaves work. Just 'key', please.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands concealment and A3 supplies only negative information, but A3 asks B to accept terms rather than sustaining clear highest-status permission.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks contents; A3 gives partial assurance; B4 imposes a deadline and A5 asks for timing.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 set credible conditions on holding a secret key.

heightening.evidence: A5 narrows communication to one coded word after B4 collection requirement.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard key and flatmate plus B4 return time establish the practical task.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 nothing alive is a pointed evasion, but question-details preface crowds the bargaining.
